decisions.quote:
That said, this is still substantially less content than would be expected if equal attention were paid to each of the four CBM categories (25%) or if the recommendations of experienced trainers were followed (33.75%).
While, in their review of CBM PD materials, Espin et al. found the greatest proportion of attention was given to conducting CBM (53%) followed by general CBM information (24%), in the case of practitioner journal content, the greatest proportion of text was devoted to general CBM information (42.16%) followed by information on conducting CBM (39.29%).
decisions.location: Original-specific primary comparison, raw chars[47988,48560); complete exact primary slice
decisions.reason: The replication confirms the central underrepresentation of DBDM found by Espin et al. (2021), but explicitly contrasts the relative ordering of the primary content categories (general CBM information vs. conducting CBM) as well as the proportion of the CBM Other category. Under the codebook rules, when a paper confirms one tested comparison while explicitly marking others as differing from the original without a superseding whole-replication verdict, the outcome is mixed.
